method: read the artifact from disk in full; hashed before and after; checked (a) class leakage across C0/C2 and SCC/WCC, (b) conclusion inflation, (c) assumption completeness, (d) decidability of the falsifier, (e) fields two competent readers could instantiate non-equivalently. The genericity transfer claim was checked against the definitions of comeagre and open dense independently.
score_scale: 0-5, one reviewer's dimensional judgement; not a universal score
score_rationale: Best class discipline in the three schemas reviewed so far: C0 is frozen, WCC content is excluded from the conclusion, the negation normal form is correct, and the tier-1 falsifier correctly requires non-meagerness rather than a single witness. Not acceptable yet: one elementary mathematical claim in the genericity transfer table is false and the variant it governs (open_dense_escape) is undefined, so a class-defining genericity statement is not pinned; plus three medium definitional ambiguities.
hard_failure_note: No HF-01..HF-13 is triggered. F2b-16-01 is an elementary falsehood inside metadata that the current taxonomy does not name; recommend an HF for false elementary mathematical claims in class-defining fields (transfer tables, genericity kinds).

findings.criterion: (e) reader disagreement + mathematical correctness of a class-defining field
findings.statement: The transfer row {pair: [open_dense_escape, residual_comeager], direction: no_transfer, witness: 'open dense does not imply comeager', status: elementary} (l.177) is false as written. An open dense set U is comeagre: comeagre means containing a countable intersection of open dense sets, and U contains itself. The complement of a nonempty open dense set is closed with empty interior, so it is nowhere dense and in particular cannot be dense. The failed direction is the reverse: a comeagre set need not be open (e.g. R minus Q in R). Separately, open_dense_escape is never formally defined: l.173 and l.179 only label it 'strictly_weaker' and 'is_this_class: false' without saying which set (good or failing) is open dense.
findings.why_it_matters: genericity.is_part_of_class is true (l.172), so the transfer table and variant strengths are class-defining. A reader cannot decide whether the open-dense variant weakens, strengthens, or contradicts the class statement, and the only witness offered is a false elementary claim. Under the natural reading (the good set is open dense) the variant is strictly stronger, not weaker; under the exceptional-set reading it is incompatible with residual rather than merely weaker.
findings.required_change: Define open_dense_escape explicitly (which set is open dense). Correct the row to residual_comeager -> open_dense_escape: no_transfer with witness 'a comeagre set need not be open; R minus Q is comeagre and not open', and if open_dense_escape denotes an open dense good set, record open_dense_escape -> residual_comeager: entails. Re-derive the statement_strength label at l.179 from the definition. The same false witness appears in the F1 genericity table and should be corrected there by its owner.

findings.statement: l.159 asserts H2_loc 'lies strictly between C2 and C0' as extension classes, i.e. C2-extensions subset H2_loc-extensions subset C0-extensions. If that ordering is asserted, then 'no proper future C0 extension' entails 'no proper future H2_loc extension' elementarily. Yet implication_ledger.one_way_entailments marks exactly that entailment unresolved (l.242), while l.245 relies on the same containment to forbid the converse transfer.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader cannot tell whether the schema asserts the containment or leaves it open; two readers will produce different implication ledgers from the same artifact.
findings.required_change: Either pin the entailment as elementary (consistent with l.159) or explain the precise obstruction that makes the containment direction unproven, and make l.245 cite that same decision.

findings.criterion: (e) reader disagreement in the extension predicate
findings.statement: extension_predicate(c) allows M' to be merely a connected time-orientable topological 4-manifold, and topology.extension_topology says M' is 'not assumed smooth'. A continuous Lorentzian metric is standardly a continuous section of the symmetric 2-tensor bundle, which needs at least a smooth (or C1) structure; in the purely topological category the notion is not standard, and some topological 4-manifolds admit no smooth structure at all.
findings.why_it_matters: The class is defined by excluding extensions; if the extension category is not standard, two readers can disagree whether a given (M',g') is even an admissible member. F2b forbids 'M' smooth with twice-differentiable metric' (l.121), which does not forbid a smooth M' with a merely continuous metric.
findings.required_change: Pin the category: standard low-regularity practice takes M' smooth (or C1) with g' continuous; state that explicitly, or define tensor fields on the topological manifold. Keep the frozen regularity of g' at C0 either way.

findings.statement: D0 admits two regularity settings: (i) smooth-with-decay with pointwise rates O(r^-1)/O(r^-2), and (ii) H^s_delta with s>5/2, delta in (1/2,1). l.154 additionally makes conformal regularity k>=3 at I+ 'part of the assumption'. It is not stated whether the pointwise decay rates are also required in setting (ii), nor how k>=3 interacts with delta in (1/2,1).
findings.why_it_matters: The two settings may define different data spaces, and a reader cannot tell which data satisfy the class. The Sobolev weight delta<1 permits slower falloff than the pointwise r^-1 rate.
findings.required_change: State whether the pointwise decay is a consequence, a requirement, or replaced by the weighted norm in setting (ii); mark k>=3 as theorem-consequence or assumption and give its source. If unresolved, add it to unresolved_items.

findings.statement: The schema never states that no symmetry is assumed. The sibling F1 schema carries symmetry: none_assumed; F2b's class_components, topology and data_class have no symmetry slot, and genericity does not explicitly say that symmetric data are meagre.
findings.why_it_matters: SCC statements are sensitive to symmetry assumptions (spherical symmetry changes the problem), so the absence of the slot is a completeness gap even if GEN excludes symmetric data implicitly.
findings.required_change: Add symmetry: none_assumed and, if intended, note that symmetric data form a meagre subset of the declared data space.

findings.statement: adm_mass.sign asserts m_ADM >= 0 'by the positive mass theorem' with citation_status unresolved and identifier null; the positive mass theorem requires completeness and decay hypotheses that are not quoted.
findings.why_it_matters: The PMT is cited as a fact used in the data class; if its hypotheses are not met by the Sobolev setting, the sign claim is unsupported.
findings.required_change: Add the PMT locator and the hypotheses it needs that the class supplies, or demote the sign to a consequence requiring proof under the declared spaces.
